push.comment.liked.note: Body of a push notification on the phone or in the browser. Its title, shown above this text and not part of it, is the name of the friend who did it: the friend liked a comment you wrote on a post. Write it as what the friend did, the friend being the subject.

push.friend.accepted.note: Body of a push notification. Its title, shown above this text and not part of it, is the name of the friend who did it: they accepted the friend request you sent them. Write it as what the friend did, the friend being the subject.

push.friend.request.note: Body of a push notification. Its title, shown above this text and not part of it, is the name of the person who did it: they asked to be your friend on Off The Cloud. Write it as what that person did, the person being the subject.

push.offline.body.text: Your device appears to have gone offline
push.offline.body.note: Body of the push notification the bridge sends when the owner's Off The Cloud device has had no connection to it for a minute. Its title is the product name, Off The Cloud. No final full stop in English.

push.post.commented.note: Body of a push notification. Its title, shown above this text and not part of it, is the name of the friend who did it: the friend wrote a comment on one of your posts. Write it as what the friend did, the friend being the subject.

push.post.liked.note: Body of a push notification. Its title, shown above this text and not part of it, is the name of the friend who did it: the friend liked one of your posts. Write it as what the friend did, the friend being the subject.

push.post.new.note: Body of a push notification. Its title, shown above this text and not part of it, is the name of the friend who did it: the friend shared a new post. Write it as what the friend did, the friend being the subject. Never more specific: a push may not say what was posted.

push.raid.stopped_bottom.text: The disk in the bottom blue USB port failed. Your files are safe on the other one: replace it soon.
push.raid.stopped_bottom.note: Body of the push notification sent when one of the device's two storage disks (a mirror: each holds a copy of every file) stops working. The device has two blue USB ports, one above the other; this disk is in the bottom one. The title is push.raid.stopped_title.

push.raid.stopped_title.note: Title of the push notification sent when one of the device's two storage disks (a mirror: each holds a copy of every file) stops working.

push.raid.stopped_top.text: The disk in the top blue USB port failed. Your files are safe on the other one: replace it soon.
push.raid.stopped_top.note: Body of the push notification sent when one of the device's two storage disks (a mirror: each holds a copy of every file) stops working. The device has two blue USB ports, one above the other; this disk is in the top one. The title is push.raid.stopped_title.

push.raid.stopped_unknown.text: One of the two storage disks failed. Your files are safe on the other one: replace it soon.
push.raid.stopped_unknown.note: Body of the push notification sent when one of the device's two storage disks (a mirror: each holds a copy of every file) stops working and the device can't tell which USB port it is in. The title is push.raid.stopped_title.

push.raid.stopped_working_bottom.text: One of the two storage disks failed. Your files are safe on the one in the bottom blue USB port: replace the other one soon.
push.raid.stopped_working_bottom.note: Body of the push notification sent when one of the device's two storage disks (a mirror: each holds a copy of every file) stops working, the device can't tell which, but can tell which still works: the device has two blue USB ports, one above the other, and the disk in the bottom one still works. The title is push.raid.stopped_title.

push.raid.stopped_working_top.text: One of the two storage disks failed. Your files are safe on the one in the top blue USB port: replace the other one soon.
push.raid.stopped_working_top.note: Body of the push notification sent when one of the device's two storage disks (a mirror: each holds a copy of every file) stops working, the device can't tell which, but can tell which still works: the device has two blue USB ports, one above the other, and the disk in the top one still works. The title is push.raid.stopped_title.

push.raid.working_body.text: The mirror is complete: every file is on both disks again.
push.raid.working_body.note: Body of the push notification sent when both storage disks work again after one had stopped: each disk holds a copy of every file again. The title is push.raid.working_title.

push.raid.working_title.note: Title of the push notification sent when both of the device's storage disks work again after one had stopped.

push.storage.full_body.text: Free some space: once it is full, new photos and files can't be saved.
push.storage.full_body.note: Body of the push notification sent when the device's storage disks are nearly full, under push.storage.full_title.

push.storage.full_title.note: Title of the push notification sent when the device's storage disks are nearly full (98% or more).

push.update.critical_body.note: Body of the push notification for a critical update to the device's software, under push.update.critical_title. Settings is the Settings screen of the Off The Cloud apps, where the update is installed. In English the release's own summary comes before this sentence; other languages show only this sentence (release summaries stay English).

push.update.critical_body_container.text: To install it, run docker compose pull and docker compose up -d on your server.
push.update.critical_body_container.note: Body of the push notification for a critical update to the device's software, under push.update.critical_title, on a device that runs in Docker (a container on the owner's home server or NAS), in place of push.update.critical_body. docker compose pull and docker compose up -d are commands typed on that server: keep them exactly as they are. In English the release's own summary comes before this sentence; other languages show only this sentence.

push.update.critical_title.text: Critical update {version} - please install it soon
push.update.critical_title.note: Title of the push notification sent when a critical update (a security fix, or one the apps need to keep working) is available for the device's software. {version} is the release's version label, such as 2.4.
